vulnerabilities.description: Insecure use of os.system() for installing packages. os.system() spawns a shell and is vulnerable to command injection. Should use subprocess.run() or subprocess.check_call() with argument arrays instead.

Insecure use of os.system() for installing packages. os.system() spawns a shell and is vulnerable to command injection. Should use subprocess.run() or subprocess.check_call() with argument arrays instead.
Insecure use of os.system() with f-string containing sys.executable. Vulnerable to command injection if sys.executable is compromised or contains spaces. Use subprocess module with argument arrays.

Session data including potentially sensitive context stored in plaintext JSON files without encryption. Vulnerable if .claude-flow directory is accessible. Consider encrypting sensitive session context or using secure session storage.

User-provided keys and values stored in plaintext JSON without input sanitization. No access control or encryption. Could be exploited if memory is accessed in a web context or template rendering scenario. Validate all input.

Race condition possible on concurrent memory access. File-based storage without locking could lead to data corruption or loss if accessed concurrently. Consider implementing file locking or atomic operations.
Temporary file created without explicit restrictive permissions (mode 0600). Permissions depend on system umask. Should use fs.writeFileSync with explicit mode to ensure secure permissions.
Hardcoded test API key 'sk-dummy' used in tests. While this is a dummy key for testing, ensure test fixtures never use real API keys. Good practice here but worth monitoring.

recommendations: CRITICAL: Replace all os.system() calls with subprocess.run() or subprocess.check_call() using argument arrays. This eliminates command injection vulnerability class entirely.
CRITICAL: Replace os.system() in cli.py lines 13-14 with: subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, '-m', 'pip', 'install', 'click']) and similar for PyGithub
HIGH: Implement encryption for session context data in session.js. Consider using a library like crypto-js or encrypting sensitive fields before storage.
HIGH: Add access control (file permissions 0600) and encryption to memory.json storage. Validate and sanitize all keys before storing.
MEDIUM: Add file locking mechanism to prevent race conditions in session.js and memory.js. Use advisory locking (fcntl on Unix, LockFile on Windows).
MEDIUM: Set restrictive permissions (0600) when creating temporary files in github-safe.js: fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, body, {mode: 0o600})
LOW: Continue to use dummy test keys (like 'sk-dummy') in tests. Never use real API keys in test fixtures or version control.
LOW: Add .env files to .gitignore (appears already present based on comments) and use environment variables exclusively for secrets.
AUDIT: Review all subprocess.Popen() and subprocess.check_call() calls to ensure shell=False (which is the default and safe) and that arguments are passed as arrays, not concatenated strings.
AUDIT: Check if any user input can reach os.system() calls in check_requirements.py or any other files through argument parsing or configuration loading.
